title: Cobalt-free high-energy cathodes
bottleneck: Removing cobalt from high-energy cathodes without losing capacity, voltage, or cycle life is still unsolved: lithium iron phosphate is safe and cheap but tops out near 190 Wh/kg at cell level, while high-manganese and disordered-rocksalt alternatives suffer from voltage fade, poor conductivity, or oxygen loss. No cobalt-free chemistry yet matches nickel-cobalt performance across all metrics simultaneously.
why_it_blocks: Cobalt supply is geographically concentrated, price-volatile, and tied to artisanal mining concerns, making it the riskiest link in battery supply chains. Without a drop-in cobalt-free high-energy cathode, EV cost reduction and supply security both stall.
current_state: LMFP (manganese-doped LFP) is commercializing with modest energy gains, and sodium-ion chemistries sidestep the issue for stationary storage. But the high-energy cobalt-free cathode that premium EVs need remains a materials research problem, not a product.
